title: Move Steam games to an external drive on Mac
observation: A Mac user wanted to free internal space by moving installed Steam games. Replies used Steam library folders and Move Install Folder, and one user said Steam sometimes forgot the external location.
product_implication: Treat a moved library as owner-registered state and verify that Steam still resolves it after restart and remount.
quality_note: Direct first-person Steam for Mac thread with concrete owner workflow and a reported persistence failure.

title: Move an entire Steam library to an external drive
observation: A MacBook Air user copied a library to an external drive, then hit read and write errors before Steam could verify the files.
product_implication: Check volume format, permissions, copy completion, and owner verification before offering to remove the source copy.
quality_note: Direct Steam for Mac report. Peer instructions are not treated as owner documentation.

title: Steam reports insufficient space for small installs on Mac
observation: A Mac user saw an insufficient-space error for games smaller than the reported free space and could not select a new library folder.
product_implication: Do not infer reclaim safety from a launcher error alone. Compare APFS free space, the target library, and Steam inventory.
quality_note: Direct first-person report with specific free-space and path symptoms.

title: Steam download and update consumed more Mac space than expected
observation: Mac users reported installs taking much more temporary space than the listed download and external drives being rejected as too small after a client update.
product_implication: Show installed size, download size, patch staging, and target-volume headroom as separate values.
quality_note: Direct Steam for Mac thread with several first-person reports. It does not establish prevalence.

title: Steam lost a symlinked external game library
observation: A Mac user moved steamapps to an external drive through a symbolic link, but Steam showed the games as not downloaded.
product_implication: Classify a symlink as a dependency. A missing target must not turn the source record into an orphan recommendation.
quality_note: Direct first-person Mac report with the failed symlink state.

title: Steam could not write to an existing external Mac library
observation: A long-used external Steam library became read-only to the client and its games were no longer recognized. A later reply restored access through macOS Full Disk Access.
product_implication: Separate unavailable, permission-blocked, and deleted states. Do not recommend reclaim while the volume is mounted but denied to Steam.
quality_note: Direct first-person Steam for Mac report with a confirmed permission remedy.

title: Mac user considered one-game-at-a-time deletion before moving Steam
observation: A MacBook user with a small SSD considered deleting and redownloading each large game, then explored moving steamapps and using a symbolic link.
product_implication: Show redownload cost and offer owner-managed relocation before deletion when the game payload is replaceable but large.
quality_note: Direct first-person Steam for Mac planning thread.

title: Steam games failed on a case-sensitive external Mac volume
observation: A Mac user installed six games externally to save internal space, but games rejected the case-sensitive filesystem or failed to find expected data.
product_implication: Require filesystem compatibility and a successful launch check before declaring an external move complete.
quality_note: Direct first-person Steam for Mac report with explicit filesystem errors.

title: Steam screenshot storage on Mac was hard to locate
observation: A Mac user could not find Steam screenshot settings while replies described a selectable uncompressed-copy folder and a separate screenshot shortcut.
product_implication: Treat screenshots as user-created data and distinguish Steam's managed copy from an optional uncompressed copy.
quality_note: Direct Steam for Mac support thread. Peer instructions may be version-sensitive.

title: Steam Cloud did not carry saves between macOS and Windows
observation: A user tested several games and found that saves or edits did not sync reliably between macOS and Windows despite cloud sync being enabled.
product_implication: Never classify a local save as safely replaceable only because Steam Cloud is enabled. Check per-game sync state and local freshness.
quality_note: Direct first-person Steam for Mac report with several named game tests.

title: Roguebook Mac cloud path change lost track of saves
observation: The game maker said a Mac Steam Cloud change caused the game to lose track of local saves in alternate Application Support folders and published recovery steps.
product_implication: Use game-specific save roots and treat duplicate-looking save folders as possible recovery branches until the game validates one.
quality_note: First-party developer notice on the owner's Steam forum. It is product evidence, not user prevalence evidence.

title: Steam screenshot folder setting created copies, not a relocation
observation: A user expected the chosen screenshot folder to replace Steam's storage, then learned that Steam still kept managed screenshots under userdata and used the chosen folder for copies.
product_implication: Do not collapse same-image files into duplicates until their owner roles and upload workflow are known.
quality_note: Direct Steam community report. Windows paths make it an adjacent storage-role example.

title: Steam Storage Manager media was local screenshot data
observation: A user assumed Steam media might be cloud-backed save data, then matched its size to locally stored compressed screenshots while separate uncompressed copies lived elsewhere.
product_implication: Label media by owner role and cloud status. A cloud icon must not imply that every local copy is disposable.
quality_note: Direct Steam help thread with a concrete size comparison. It is not Mac-specific.

title: Steam Cloud storage and macOS save roots
observation: Steam documents per-game cloud quotas, local synchronization before and after play, macOS roots under home, Application Support, and Documents, plus root overrides for cross-platform saves.
product_implication: Model cloud configuration and local paths separately. Preserve local files when sync status, root overrides, or game support are unknown.
quality_note: Current first-party Steamworks documentation.

title: Steam Workshop content model
observation: Steam Workshop ties downloadable user-generated content to app IDs, item IDs, subscriptions, and owner APIs rather than a plain folder alone.
product_implication: Classify Workshop files as subscription-backed content and use Steam's item inventory before suggesting manual folder deletion.
quality_note: Current first-party Steamworks documentation.

title: Steam Workshop installation and update lifecycle
observation: Steam documents subscribed-item download, installation state, update state, content folders, and explicit item removal through Workshop APIs.
product_implication: Use item state and subscription identity to tell a complete install from staging, an update, or an unsubscribed leftover.
quality_note: Current first-party implementation guide.

title: Steam screenshot ownership and library integration
observation: Steam exposes screenshot capture and library integration through an owner API, with screenshots attached to games and user metadata.
product_implication: Protect screenshot files and their metadata as user-created records, even when the game payload is replaceable.
quality_note: Current first-party Steamworks documentation.

title: SteamPipe depots, builds, and local content
observation: Steam distributes game payloads as depots and builds through SteamPipe, with manifests and chunk-based content rather than one monolithic installer artifact.
product_implication: Treat installed depots, manifest state, and patch staging as separate storage roles that Steam can usually repair or redownload.
quality_note: Current first-party Steamworks documentation.

title: External Unreal Engine installs crashed on a full MacBook
observation: A Mac user installed several Unreal Engine versions externally because the internal drive was full, but each install crashed during initialization.
product_implication: Do not equate an external copy with a valid move. Require owner recognition and a successful launch before source cleanup.
quality_note: Direct first-person Epic forum report with Mac paths and versions.

title: Epic Launcher did not recognize a shared Mac lab install
observation: Mac lab users could launch a shared Unreal install directly, but Epic Launcher asked each account to reinstall into the nonempty directory and could not see projects.
product_implication: Track owner registration per user account. Shared readable files may still be unregistered for the current launcher profile.
quality_note: Direct first-person Epic forum report from two Mac labs.

title: Epic Launcher logs consumed Mac disk space
observation: A Mac user reported the launcher logging process names fast enough to consume disk space and make Console lag.
product_implication: Classify repeating launcher logs as reviewable diagnostics, but verify the process is stopped and show the exact log path before removal.
quality_note: Direct first-person Epic forum report with attached diagnostic context.

title: Epic reported no space despite 136 GB free on Mac
observation: A MacBook user reported that Unreal Engine installation stopped immediately for insufficient space while macOS showed 136.25 GB free.
product_implication: Treat launcher free-space errors as diagnostics, not proof that unrelated files should be deleted.
quality_note: Direct first-person Epic forum report with an exact free-space figure.

title: Stale shared folders blocked Epic Launcher installation on Mac
observation: A Mac user traced repeated launcher installation failure to an existing shared UnrealEngine folder and described a clean install path that worked.
product_implication: Mark stale owner state separately from game payloads. Confirm the owner no longer references it before any cleanup offer.
quality_note: Direct first-person Epic forum report with a reproducible shared path.

title: Epic Launcher cache deletion restored its Mac interface
observation: A Mac user reinstalled and restarted without success, then restored the launcher by removing its cache. Other Mac users confirmed the result.
product_implication: Offer owner-documented web-cache cleanup as low recovery-cost only after the launcher exits and the exact cache path is resolved.
quality_note: Direct first-person Epic forum report with several confirmations. It does not prove universal safety for all Epic data.

title: Moved Fortnite files left Epic with stale free-space state on Mac
observation: A Mac user manually reorganized Fortnite and Unreal files, after which Epic no longer recognized the install and kept reporting an old free-space value through reinstalls.
product_implication: Detect manual moves and stale owner manifests before labeling either copy as unused. Prefer owner repair or re-import.
quality_note: Direct first-person Epic forum report with the sequence that created the stale state.

title: Epic Launcher could not find an external Unreal install
observation: A user moved an Unreal install to an external drive for use on another machine, but Epic asked for a new install and refused the existing nonempty directory.
product_implication: An intact folder without matching launcher state is not safe proof of either active use or orphan status.
quality_note: Direct Epic forum report. The post does not identify macOS, so it is an adjacent owner-state example.

title: Clear Epic Games Launcher webcache on Mac
observation: Epic directs Mac users to quit the launcher and remove webcache under ~/Library/Caches/com.epicgames.EpicGamesLauncher before relaunching.
product_implication: This exact owner cache can be a low-risk candidate after process and path checks, but Tessera must still require confirmation.
quality_note: Current first-party Epic support procedure.

title: Change Epic Games Launcher installation directory
observation: Epic says changing the launcher location may require uninstall and reinstall, and warns that uninstalling the launcher removes installed games on some platforms.
product_implication: Do not treat the launcher app as independent from its managed game inventory. Show owner side effects before any uninstall plan.
quality_note: Current first-party Epic support documentation.

title: Move an Epic-installed game to another directory
observation: Epic's move workflow makes a backup, uninstalls the owner record, starts a small new download, restores files, and lets the launcher verify them.
product_implication: Tessera should not delete the source copy until Epic completes verification and launches the moved game.
quality_note: Current first-party Epic support procedure. The shown path is PC-focused but the ownership sequence is relevant.

title: Epic cannot automatically detect every prior install
observation: Epic says the launcher has no general feature to detect prior game files and documents a partial-download workaround that may not work for every game.
product_implication: An unregistered game directory needs owner repair or a manual user decision, not automatic orphan deletion.
quality_note: Current first-party Epic support documentation.

title: Enable Epic cloud saves
observation: Epic documents a global cloud-save setting and warns that changing it across machines can create cloud-save conflicts.
product_implication: Cloud enabled is not enough to mark a local save replaceable. Check per-game support and unresolved conflicts.
quality_note: Current first-party Epic support documentation.

title: Epic uninstall can remove local saves
observation: Epic says uninstall may delete saves inside the install location when a game lacks cloud-save support and advises backing them up first.
product_implication: Scan install roots for saves and require a backup or cloud proof before proposing game uninstall.
quality_note: Current first-party Epic support documentation.

title: Epic update size, verification, and Mac webcache
observation: Epic separates file verification from cache cleanup, says verification repairs changed files without affecting saves, and gives the Mac webcache path.
product_implication: Distinguish repairable game chunks from saves and from launcher cache. Each needs a different reclaim action.
quality_note: Current first-party Epic support documentation.

title: GOG GALAXY did not rescan an external game library
observation: After reboot, a user saw only part of an external GOG library and sought a full rescan; replies described scan folders and per-game import.
product_implication: Treat missing owner inventory after remount as an import problem until GALAXY scans or the user confirms abandonment.
quality_note: Direct GOG forum report. Windows drive-letter details make this adjacent to macOS.

title: Moving GOG games to an external SSD required re-import
observation: Users copied games externally, changed the default install folder, and then imported each game so GALAXY changed its state from Install to Play.
product_implication: A file copy and an owner import are separate checkpoints. Source deletion must wait for both.
quality_note: Direct GOG GALAXY forum reports. The thread is Windows-focused.

title: A GOG GALAXY debug log filled a system drive
observation: A user reported GALAXY consuming about 40 GB rapidly, and replies traced similar cases to a runaway debug log.
product_implication: Surface repeating logs as a distinct low-recovery-cost class after verifying the owning launcher is stopped.
quality_note: Direct GOG forum report. It is an adjacent Windows example and does not prove the same path on macOS.

title: Uninstall a game through GOG GALAXY
observation: GOG documents owner-managed game uninstall through GALAXY rather than raw folder deletion.
product_implication: Prefer the launcher uninstall command and separately protect saves, mods, and screenshots that may sit inside or beside the game folder.
quality_note: First-party GOG support documentation.

title: Back up GOG cloud saves
observation: GOG provides a separate cloud-save backup procedure, which confirms that cloud availability and a user-held backup are different states.
product_implication: Record backup proof before treating local saves as recoverable from cloud.
quality_note: First-party GOG support documentation.

title: GOG GALAXY storage and import error classes
observation: GOG separates not-enough-space, import, library removal, local executable, uninstall, and cloud-sync failures into different error classes.
product_implication: Map each GALAXY failure to its owner state. Do not turn every error into a generic delete recommendation.
quality_note: First-party GOG support section.

title: Remove saves from GOG cloud
observation: GOG treats cloud-save removal as a separate owner action from deleting local game data.
product_implication: Never infer that deleting a local save also clears cloud copies, or that a cloud deletion is reversible.
quality_note: First-party GOG support documentation.

title: Delete local GOG GALAXY data
observation: GOG documents local GALAXY data deletion separately from account deletion, installed games, and cloud state.
product_implication: Show the scope of each owner data store before asking for confirmation. Local launcher cleanup must not imply account or game deletion.
quality_note: First-party GOG support documentation.

title: Disable GOG cloud saves
observation: GOG exposes cloud-save control as a product setting rather than a property of every local save folder.
product_implication: Store per-game cloud support and current sync state. Do not use a global setting as deletion proof.
quality_note: First-party GOG support documentation.

title: Choose GOG install and download locations
observation: GOG distinguishes the game installation destination from the location used to download files.
product_implication: Classify downloadable installers and installed payloads as separate roles with different recovery costs.
quality_note: First-party GOG support documentation.

title: GOG GALAXY troubleshooting state list
observation: GOG's owner support separates a missing game, corrupt game data, inaccessible drive, and out-of-space state.
product_implication: Use distinct state labels and owner repair actions instead of a single orphan label.
quality_note: First-party GOG support section.

title: Battle.net failed to reinstall on Mac until shared folders were copied
observation: A Mac user restored Battle.net by copying the app and /Users/Shared/Battle.net and Blizzard folders from another Mac through an external drive.
product_implication: Treat shared Battle.net folders as owner state tied to the app. An apparently stale shared folder may be required for recovery.
quality_note: Direct first-person Blizzard forum report with exact Mac paths.

title: Battle.net stayed on calculating size for an external install
observation: A user could not start an external Battle.net install because size calculation never completed; support replied that external drives can cause install and update failures.
product_implication: Do not recommend an external relocation without a launcher-supported target and a completed size and launch check.
quality_note: Direct Blizzard forum report. The operating system is not clear, so this is adjacent evidence.

title: Mac user needed WoW add-ons and settings on a new PC
observation: A Mac user planned to redownload WoW but copy Interface/AddOns and WTF/Accounts to preserve the configured UI and add-on state.
product_implication: Classify add-ons and their settings as separate user-owned layers. The game payload is replaceable; the configured state may not be.
quality_note: Direct first-person WoW forum report with a Mac source machine and named folders.

title: WoW user moved the game but protected add-on configuration
observation: A user moving WoW between drives wanted to preserve heavily configured add-ons; replies identified Interface and WTF as the critical folders.
product_implication: Exclude mod settings and macros from generic game-folder cleanup unless the user explicitly includes them.
quality_note: Direct WoW forum report. It is not Mac-specific.

title: WoW player wanted to back up years of UI work
observation: A player asked whether copying AddOns, WTF, and Screenshots to an external drive was allowed because the UI represented years of work.
product_implication: Assign high recovery value to configured UI, macros, and screenshots even when their byte size is small.
quality_note: Direct first-person WoW forum report. It expresses user value but is not Mac-specific.

title: WoW user separated backups from rebuildable cache
observation: A user asked which WoW folders to back up. The thread distinguished Screenshots, Interface, and WTF from cache and the redownloadable game install.
product_implication: Present caches, user configuration, add-ons, screenshots, and game data as separate reclaim classes.
quality_note: Direct WoW forum report. Peer descriptions are useful but not owner documentation.

title: Mac WoW repair could redownload Data without touching add-ons
observation: Mac troubleshooting separated the redownloadable WoW Data folder from Interface/AddOns and WTF settings, which users were told to back up first.
product_implication: Use known internal roles to offer payload repair while protecting add-ons and configuration.
quality_note: Direct Mac Technical Support thread with exact folder boundaries.

title: Mac WoW reinstall preserved three user folders
observation: Mac users discussed reinstalling WoW while backing up and restoring WTF, Interface, and Screenshots because those held the valuable personal state.
product_implication: A game reinstall plan must name the protected folders before any source deletion.
quality_note: Direct Mac Technical Support thread with repeated folder-level recovery advice.

title: WoW folders on macOS 11 were outside the app bundle
observation: A new Mac user searched inside the WoW app bundle for Interface and WTF, but the active folders were beside the app under the retail directory.
product_implication: Resolve the live owner path before classifying bundle contents or nearby folders. Similar names can belong to different roles.
quality_note: Direct first-person Mac forum report with the resolved path.

title: WoW drive migration split payload from settings and screenshots
observation: A player moving WoW to a new drive identified WTF, Interface, and Screenshots as the parts worth preserving even if the game client was reinstalled.
product_implication: Offer a preserve-and-redownload plan that protects user work while reclaiming the large payload.
quality_note: Direct WoW forum report. It is not Mac-specific.

title: Delete Battle.net owner state on Mac
observation: Blizzard identifies /Users/Shared/Battle.net/Agent, agent.db, and the Battle.net shared folder as repair targets and warns that deleting them can make the app forget game locations.
product_implication: Owner-state cleanup must warn that installed games may appear missing and provide Locate this game as the recovery path.
quality_note: First-party Blizzard support documentation with exact Mac paths.

title: Uninstall games through Battle.net
observation: Blizzard documents owner-managed game uninstall and says player data for supported games remains on Blizzard servers, while leftover local files may remain.
product_implication: Separate server-held progress from local screenshots, add-ons, settings, and game-specific saves before reclaim.
quality_note: First-party Blizzard support documentation.

title: Delete the Battle.net cache folder
observation: Blizzard publishes a separate procedure for removing Battle.net cache so the owner app can rebuild it.
product_implication: Classify this cache as rebuildable only when the path matches the active owner version and Battle.net is closed.
quality_note: First-party Blizzard support documentation.

title: Reset game folder permissions on Mac
observation: Blizzard treats Mac game-folder permission failure as a repair problem for the folder and enclosed files.
product_implication: A permission-denied tree is not an orphan. Offer permission repair or owner locate before deletion review.
quality_note: First-party Blizzard support documentation linked from the current Mac support index.

title: Check case-sensitive volumes for Blizzard games on Mac
observation: Blizzard identifies case-sensitive volumes as a cause of Mac installation problems.
product_implication: Check filesystem compatibility before relocation and do not delete a source install until the target passes owner validation.
quality_note: First-party Blizzard support documentation linked from the current Mac support index.

title: itch install failed when the expected Mac Applications path was missing
observation: A macOS install failed when ~/Applications did not exist, and another case failed when itch.app existed but setup state.json did not.
product_implication: Pair app presence with owner setup metadata. One without the other is a repair state, not automatic clutter.
quality_note: Direct issue in the owner's tracker with exact paths.

title: itch could reinstall but not update a bundled Mac game
observation: A developer's signed .app game launched when downloaded directly, but itch could not update it in place; uninstall and clean reinstall worked.
product_implication: Distinguish patch failure from corrupt payload. Preserve saves and owner metadata before proposing a reinstall.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with a macOS packaging change and workaround.

title: itch external install paths need compatible filesystems
observation: The owner issue records extraction to a staged archive on an incompatible external filesystem and proposes blocking unsupported install paths.
product_implication: Validate filesystem features before relocating or extracting game content.
quality_note: Maintainer implementation issue in the owner repository. It is product evidence, not user evidence.

title: Clearing itch cache and user data did not fix a Mac launch crash
observation: A Mac user tried uninstall, reinstall, cache cleanup, and user-data cleanup, but a launcher crash remained.
product_implication: Cache cleanup must be presented as a scoped repair, not a guaranteed fix or a reason to erase broader user data.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with attempted remedies.

title: itch sandbox hid a RenPy save on macOS
observation: A Mac player lost visible progress when sandboxing blocked RenPy from its normal save path under Library, even though the storage issue was path access rather than a deleted game.
product_implication: Treat save visibility changes across sandbox modes as alternate roots. Never delete one root until the game opens the expected save.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with a denied save path.

title: itch user installed games to the wrong Library location
observation: A user accidentally installed many items to the default ~/Library location and wanted an owner-managed way to move them to another registered install location.
product_implication: Offer relocate and verify before delete. Accidental placement does not make installed games unnecessary.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with the Mac default path.

title: itch kept versioned butler files under Application Support
observation: A Mac user found butler downloaded under Application Support/itch/broth/versions but missing from the apps link expected by the launcher.
product_implication: Versioned launcher tools may be active dependencies. Confirm the selected runtime and links before pruning old-looking versions.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with exact runtime paths.

title: Deleting an itch app forced Mac trust setup again
observation: A Mac report noted that deleting and restoring an unsigned app repeated the manual trust action required by macOS.
product_implication: Record code-signing and quarantine state as compatibility state. Redownload may not restore the prior trusted launch state automatically.
quality_note: Direct owner issue with a Mac reinstall consequence.

title: itch sandbox launch failed for a Java game on Mac
observation: A Mac user reported that a Java game ran outside the itch sandbox but failed inside it because the sandbox launch path could not find a class.
product_implication: Preserve per-game launch and sandbox settings. A game folder alone is not the complete runnable object.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with a controlled sandbox comparison.

title: itch reinstall should repair bundle permissions
observation: A maintainer issue says reinstall did not reconfigure a Mac bundle with missing execute permission and proposes always repairing it.
product_implication: A failed reinstall can leave owner state incomplete. Verify permissions and launch, not only file count.
quality_note: Maintainer implementation note in the owner tracker.

title: itch user wanted visible progress for multiple game downloads
observation: A user asked for system-visible progress while downloading one or more games because active download state was hard to see.
product_implication: Do not recommend deleting a large temporary object until owner activity and download progress are checked.
quality_note: Direct owner issue. It describes visibility needs rather than a Mac storage failure.

title: itch install locations
observation: itch defines registered install locations, lets users add more, and chooses the last-used location for later installs.
product_implication: Use registered locations and owner scan results before classifying game directories.
quality_note: Current first-party itch app documentation.

title: itch scans for owner metadata before importing games
observation: itch can re-import only folders with its .itch metadata and cannot identify website downloads placed there manually.
product_implication: Treat .itch metadata as ownership evidence. A folder without it needs user review, not an orphan verdict.
quality_note: Current first-party itch app documentation.

title: itch sandbox can create alternate save roots
observation: itch says sandbox modes may isolate or simulate home directories, so saves can remain on disk while becoming invisible after a mode change.
product_implication: Search all owner-defined save roots and show mode context before any save cleanup.
quality_note: Current first-party itch app documentation.

title: itch versioned dependencies under macOS Application Support
observation: itch stores downloaded runtime dependencies under ~/Library/Application Support/itch/broth and uses butler plus a SQLite database to manage installs.
product_implication: Classify owner runtimes, their versions, and the install database separately. Do not prune by age alone.
quality_note: Current first-party itch app documentation.

title: itch download compatibility and offline library
observation: itch filters downloads by platform, can show incompatible builds with a warning, and keeps the user's own library searchable offline.
product_implication: A downloaded incompatible build can still be intentionally retained. Use owner metadata and explicit user intent before reclaim.
quality_note: Current first-party itch app documentation.

title: itch per-game launch and sandbox settings
observation: itch stores per-game arguments, wrappers, environment variables, and sandbox overrides that can be required for a game to launch.
product_implication: Preserve launch configuration with the game record. A payload without its wrapper or settings may not be recoverable by redownload alone.
quality_note: Current first-party itch app documentation.

title: Heroic could not import Mac games from a shared drive
observation: A Mac user selected .app games installed on a shared drive by another launcher or Mac, but Heroic returned to the game page without importing them.
product_implication: Treat cross-machine game files as unregistered until Heroic confirms import and launch.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with a shared-drive setup.

title: Heroic downloaded a native Mac game before installation failed
observation: On macOS 15, Heroic completed the game download but then marked installation failed while a direct GOG download worked.
product_implication: Separate completed download archives from installed apps and failed staging. Offer retry or owner repair before reclaim.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with macOS version and comparison.

title: Heroic could not uninstall an Amazon game missing from disk
observation: A deleted Amazon game remained in Heroic as not available, and the owner uninstall action failed before removing the record.
product_implication: Distinguish an orphaned owner record from remaining payload. Fix inventory without searching for bytes that no longer exist.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue on macOS.

title: Heroic redownloaded an unwanted GPTK runtime
observation: A Mac user deleted an unused roughly 1 GB GPTK runtime, but Heroic downloaded it again and sometimes replaced the preferred CrossOver setting.
product_implication: Expose automatic runtime policy and stop the creation loop before offering repeated cleanup.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with size and recurrence.

title: Heroic reinstalled GPTK and changed the saved Wine choice
observation: A Mac user said each restart restored GPTK and made it the default after the user removed it and selected Wine Staging.
product_implication: A reclaim action needs a durable owner setting or the bytes will return and the compatibility choice may change.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with a repeatable restart cycle.

title: Heroic Move Game failed with the macOS rsync version
observation: Heroic's Move Game action failed on macOS because its rsync arguments were not accepted by the system version.
product_implication: Do not remove the source after a move command starts. Require an owner success result and target launch.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with the exact move-command failure.

title: A macOS username change left Heroic paths stale
observation: After the macOS account and home name changed, Heroic did not update configuration and game paths.
product_implication: Resolve path migrations before declaring missing targets orphaned. Stale absolute paths can point to live data under a renamed home.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue about macOS path persistence.

title: Heroic confused a native Mac app with its parent install folder
observation: For native games installed as a single .app, Heroic's Install Path action opened the app rather than its containing folder.
product_implication: Model app bundles as installed objects and retain the parent directory as location context.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with the native Mac bundle case.

title: Heroic could not import an Amazon game from an external drive
observation: A user moved to a new computer with games on an external drive. Heroic imported GOG and Epic installs but stopped while importing Amazon games.
product_implication: Use store-specific import checks. Success for one launcher adapter does not prove another can adopt the same files.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with cross-store comparison.

title: Heroic used the wrong Wine prefix for a GOG game on Mac
observation: A Mac user found Heroic launching a GOG game through the default ~/.wine prefix while the launcher showed another configured prefix.
product_implication: Treat prefixes as active runtime and save containers. Verify the prefix actually used by the process before reclaiming another.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with launch logs and paths.

title: Heroic expected missing helper tools under Mac Application Support
observation: A Mac report found winetricks absent under Heroic Application Support and identified other helper binaries missing from the runtime.
product_implication: Do not prune tools by unfamiliar name. Link them to compatibility actions and installed games first.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with exact helper locations.

title: Heroic game shortcut kept stale Mac metadata
observation: After a user renamed an installed game and changed its icon, Heroic created a Mac shortcut with the new name but the old icon.
product_implication: Treat shortcuts as derived owner metadata. They can be rebuilt after the canonical game and configuration are preserved.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue. It concerns small derived data, so it is adjacent evidence.

title: Heroic reported a Mac shortcut created when no file appeared
observation: Heroic displayed success for a manually added program shortcut, but no shortcut appeared in either Applications location checked by the user.
product_implication: Do not treat an owner success message as file proof. Derived launchers need path validation.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue about derived metadata.

title: Heroic needed Rosetta before compatibility tools could run
observation: Heroic actions on Apple silicon failed through helper commands when Rosetta was absent, leading to a request for an explicit warning.
product_implication: Track system compatibility dependencies outside game folders. Deleting runtime state can make intact games unusable.
quality_note: Direct owner issue. It is adjacent because Rosetta itself is system-managed storage.

title: Heroic macOS configuration, cache, and game logs
observation: Heroic documents macOS cache under ~/Library/Application Support/heroic plus separate configuration, store, GameConfig, install logs, and play logs.
product_implication: Map these subtrees by role. Cache and logs may be reviewable while settings, credentials, and game records need protection.
quality_note: Maintained owner wiki.

title: Heroic Wine and Proton prefix model
observation: Heroic passes a selected WINEPREFIX or STEAM_COMPAT_DATA_PATH and searches several locations for Wine and Proton versions.
product_implication: Treat each prefix and runtime as a dependency graph with the games, save paths, and owner settings that use it.
quality_note: Maintained owner wiki. Some Linux paths are adjacent to the Mac implementation.

title: Fully remove Heroic on Mac
observation: Heroic separates the app, config folder, installed game folder, and prefixes in its Mac removal instructions and marks game and prefix deletion as optional.
product_implication: Present these as separate confirmation groups. Removing Heroic does not imply permission to remove games or prefixes.
quality_note: Maintained owner wiki with exact Mac paths.

title: Heroic save paths can live inside Wine prefixes
observation: Heroic warns that cloud sync depends on the correct save path and that Windows game saves often live inside the Wine prefix.
product_implication: Never classify a prefix as disposable without finding game saves and checking cloud sync configuration.
quality_note: Maintained owner wiki. Workaround claims are product facts, not user evidence.

title: Heroic Mac compatibility runtimes
observation: Heroic supports several Mac compatibility layers, downloads some through its manager, and requires Rosetta for x86_64 software on Apple silicon.
product_implication: Group compatibility layers by current game use, owner setting, architecture, and redownload source before review.
quality_note: Maintained owner Mac guide.

title: Steam games installed inside a Heroic Wine prefix on Mac
observation: Heroic's Mac guide says Windows Steam games can live inside the selected prefix and warns that deleting the prefix loses all downloaded content.
product_implication: A prefix can contain the launcher, games, saves, and compatibility state. Tessera must show nested ownership before deletion.
quality_note: Pinned revision of the maintained owner wiki.

title: Moving one Whisky bottle cleared pins from all bottles
observation: Changing the default bottle path and moving one bottle cleared pinned programs across moved and unmoved bottles.
product_implication: Back up and validate the shared bottle registry before moving any bottle. A move can affect metadata outside the target.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with reproducible steps.

title: New Whisky bottles disappeared from the owner list
observation: A user created bottles that disappeared from Whisky's list immediately, leaving uncertainty about whether files remained on disk.
product_implication: Compare the bottle registry with actual Metadata.plist roots before labeling unlisted bottles as abandoned.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue.

title: Whisky bottle vanished and no Finder folder appeared
observation: A user saw a newly created bottle for about a second, then it vanished and no bottle folder appeared in Finder.
product_implication: Distinguish failed creation from orphaned storage. Do not promise space recovery when the bytes may never have been committed.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with UI and filesystem checks.

title: A Steam bottle disappeared after creation in Whisky
observation: A user's Steam bottle disappeared milliseconds after creation although the same workflow had worked the day before.
product_implication: Use registry, metadata, and directory evidence together. A missing sidebar entry does not identify safe-to-delete bytes.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue.

title: Genshin installer saw too little disk space in Whisky
observation: A user received an insufficient-space warning from a game installer inside Whisky despite choosing a destination believed to have room.
product_implication: Compare host, bottle, and Wine-reported capacity before asking the user to delete data.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with installer screenshot.

title: Whisky users could leave gigabytes of bottles after abandoning the app
observation: A user asked for a full uninstaller because people can remove or abandon Whisky without realizing that bottles remain and occupy gigabytes.
product_implication: Show app removal, registry removal, and bottle deletion as separate actions with sizes and exact paths.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner feature report about leftover storage.

title: Whisky bottle export to an external SSD lacked progress
observation: A user exporting bottles to an external SSD to free laptop space could only infer progress from the growing archive file.
product_implication: Detect active archive writes and never offer the growing file or source bottle for cleanup before export validation.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with the storage motive and active-write signal.

title: Whisky logs grew to 187 GB
observation: A user traced low disk space to Whisky logs under ~/Library/Logs/com.isaacmarovitz.Whisky, with the largest file at 187 GB and repeating msync errors.
product_implication: Prioritize bounded repeating logs for review, stop the producer, and show their low recovery value compared with bottles.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with path, size, and repeated content.

title: Whisky repeated errors into a 10 GB log
observation: A user found a 10 GB log made from the same repeating errors and asked for repeated lines to be collapsed.
product_implication: Detect low-entropy log growth and fix or stop the writer before deletion so the space stays free.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with a measured log size.

title: A Whisky game could not read its own save files
observation: A user created a world and character, saved, exited, then could not load them because the game lacked expected file access inside Whisky.
product_implication: Treat unreadable saves as recovery candidates and permission problems, not stale files.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with a save and reload sequence.

title: Wine misreported free space for a Whisky bottle on a 4 TB external drive
observation: A bottle on a 4 TB external drive with 2247 GB available reported only 47 GB to Wine and blocked a Steam game install.
product_implication: Use host filesystem capacity as the source of truth and display the compatibility layer's conflicting reading.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with exact host and guest free-space figures.

title: Steam in Whisky showed an uninstalled game still using space
observation: After uninstalling Elden Ring, Steam inside Whisky still showed its space as occupied while macOS storage did not.
product_implication: Reconcile owner inventory with filesystem allocation before offering further deletion. The stale value may represent no bytes.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with a host versus guest comparison.

title: A game in Whisky saw 5 GB free when macOS had 145 GB
observation: A game reported only 5 GB free inside Whisky while the user reported 145 GB available on the Mac.
product_implication: Do not convert guest capacity errors into cleanup pressure. Diagnose the bottle mapping first.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with exact figures.

title: Removed Whisky bottles could leave full files on disk
observation: Whisky could remove a bottle from its UI without deleting the files, after which the user had no easy way to review or restore the unregistered bottle.
product_implication: Classify unregistered bottle roots as recoverable owner state. Offer re-add, archive, or delete with exact-path confirmation.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner feature report about intentionally separated remove and delete actions.

title: Reinstalling Whisky did not restore bottle creation
observation: After a reinstall, a user got a blank app after bottle creation and could not recover normal behavior through broader cleanup attempts.
product_implication: Preserve existing bottle roots during launcher repair. Reinstall is not proof that old state is safe to remove.
quality_note: Direct first-person owner issue with reinstall history.

title: Whisky and CrossOver bottle sharing was unclear
observation: A user wanted to share bottles between Whisky and CrossOver but could not identify a supported path.
product_implication: Do not assume one Wine owner's bottle can be deleted after another owner sees the same game. Validate cross-owner import and launch.
quality_note: Direct owner issue. It is adjacent because it asks for a feature rather than reports loss.

title: Whisky bottles and shared Steam libraries
observation: Whisky defines each bottle as a self-contained Windows filesystem and recommends a separate shared Steam library so games survive bottle replacement.
product_implication: Classify the bottle and shared game library as separate owners and recovery units.
quality_note: Current first-party Whisky documentation.

title: Whisky remove and delete are different commands
observation: WhiskyCmd lists bottles from BottleVM.plist and has separate delete-from-disk and remove-from-Whisky commands, plus add from Metadata.plist.
product_implication: Mirror the owner distinction. A removed bottle can be re-registered; a deleted bottle loses its filesystem state.
quality_note: Current first-party Whisky CLI documentation.

title: Prism users wanted external instance folders from several launchers
observation: A user wanted Prism to load instances stored by several launchers without copying each instance into one owner folder.
product_implication: Detect shared or imported instance roots and avoid counting the same logical instance as safe duplicates.
quality_note: Direct owner issue. It is not Mac-specific, so it is adjacent evidence.

title: Prism appeared to lose instances when a drive was unplugged
observation: A user opened Prism while the instance drive was unplugged and then saw the instances gone, raising concern that owner state had been changed.
product_implication: An offline root must freeze cleanup and owner-record changes until the volume returns.
quality_note: Direct owner issue on Windows. It is a useful offline-volume counterexample.

title: Prism users needed several instance roots to manage drive space
observation: A player wanted important modpacks on a small fast drive and other packs on a larger drive through multiple instance folders.
product_implication: Model storage placement per instance instead of treating the launcher root as one movable block.
quality_note: Direct owner issue. It is platform-neutral adjacent evidence.

title: Changing Prism's instance folder did not imply moving its contents
observation: A user asked Prism to offer a content move when the configured instance folder changes instead of only pointing new operations elsewhere.
product_implication: Separate changing a default path from migrating existing data. Verify both before deleting the old root.
quality_note: Direct owner issue. It is platform-neutral adjacent evidence.

title: Prism instances duplicated resource and shader packs
observation: A player wanted shared resource packs and shader packs because separate instances required repeated downloads or copies.
product_implication: Identify byte-identical shared assets, but preserve instance references and use links only when the owner supports them.
quality_note: Direct owner issue. It is platform-neutral adjacent evidence.

title: Changing a Prism folder did not move the shared Minecraft payload
observation: A user with a full system drive changed the instance folder but found shared Minecraft files still on the original drive.
product_implication: Show shared assets and libraries outside instance roots. Moving instances alone may reclaim less than expected.
quality_note: Direct owner issue on Windows. It is a useful shared-payload counterexample.

title: Prism users wanted central resource and shader pack folders
observation: A player asked for central resource and shader pack folders because separate instances duplicated the same large files.
product_implication: Detect shared-content opportunities, but preserve per-instance references and owner compatibility before reclaiming copies.
quality_note: Direct owner issue. It is platform-neutral adjacent evidence.

title: Prism proposal described a cache for repeated mod downloads
observation: A user proposed caching downloaded mods and using links or copy-on-write clones to avoid duplicate files across instances.
product_implication: Classify the cache as replaceable while treating linked instance files as live dependencies, not duplicates safe to remove.
quality_note: Direct owner issue. It is a design request, not proof of current Prism behavior.

title: Prism redirect cache could persist after its purpose ended
observation: A user asked Prism to clear its redirect cache automatically because cached download redirects could become stale.
product_implication: A known owner cache can be a reviewable reclaim class, but Tessera must verify that no active install or update uses it.
quality_note: Direct owner issue. It describes requested cleanup behavior.

title: A Prism user wanted to offload mods while keeping saves and settings
observation: A user wanted to remove or offload downloadable mods from old instances while retaining saves, settings, and other personal state.
product_implication: Offer role-level choices inside an instance. Do not make users choose between keeping everything and deleting the whole instance.
quality_note: Direct owner issue. It clearly separates replaceable packages from personal state.

title: Prism could fail poorly when the disk filled during an operation
observation: A user reported poor handling when an operation ran out of disk space, leaving uncertainty about the partial result.
product_implication: Treat partial downloads and extraction output as uncertain until the owner confirms success or they are proven inactive and disposable.
quality_note: Direct owner issue. It is platform-neutral adjacent evidence.

title: A Prism log grew to several gigabytes
observation: A user reported a launcher log reaching about four gigabytes during repeated output.
product_implication: Flag unusually large logs as rebuildable candidates, stop or identify the writer first, and surface the recurrence cause.
quality_note: Direct owner issue. It is a concrete large-log case, not a prevalence claim.

title: A Prism user wanted old modpacks moved to archive storage
observation: A user wanted inactive modpacks moved to a slower archive drive without losing their launcher identity.
product_implication: An archive action must keep owner metadata, verify the target volume, and prove that the instance can be restored before source removal.
quality_note: Direct owner issue. It is adjacent evidence for cold-storage workflows.

title: Prism users wanted screenshots managed across instances
observation: A user asked for a central view of screenshots stored inside several instances.
product_implication: Discover screenshots across owner roots and classify them as user-created records, never as cache or disposable instance residue.
quality_note: Direct owner issue. It identifies a user-created asset scattered across instances.

title: Prism Launcher data location
observation: Prism documents its platform data locations and the files and folders stored under its data root.
product_implication: Use the documented root as an owner boundary, then classify its descendants by role instead of assigning one risk level to the whole root.
quality_note: First-party Prism documentation.

title: Prism Launcher settings
observation: Prism documents launcher settings that control folders, Java, downloads, and other owner state.
product_implication: Read settings before proposing moves or deletion. A configured path is stronger ownership evidence than folder-name guessing.
quality_note: First-party Prism documentation.

title: Migrating MultiMC instances into Prism Launcher
observation: Prism documents migration as moving or copying instance data into an owner-recognized location.
product_implication: A filesystem copy is not enough. Confirm that the destination owner recognizes and launches the migrated instance before deleting the source.
quality_note: First-party Prism documentation.

title: Installing loader mods in Prism Launcher
observation: Prism documents mods as instance-managed files with enablement and dependency state.
product_implication: Classify mod jars as user-selected content with owner metadata. Do not remove them as ordinary downloads without an explicit choice.
quality_note: First-party Prism documentation.

title: Copying a Prism Launcher instance
observation: Prism provides an owner operation to copy an instance and select which data is included.
product_implication: Recognize owner-created copies as intentional until byte identity, use, and user intent are checked. Duplicate size alone is not deletion proof.
quality_note: First-party Prism documentation.

title: Managing screenshots in Prism Launcher
observation: Prism documents viewing, uploading, and deleting screenshots tied to instances.
product_implication: Present screenshots as user-created assets with preview and export options. Require item-level confirmation for deletion.
quality_note: First-party Prism documentation.

title: Importing a zip instance into Prism Launcher
observation: Prism documents importing packaged instances from local files or links.
product_implication: Distinguish a source archive from the installed instance. The archive may be replaceable only after import success and provenance are known.
quality_note: First-party Prism documentation.

title: Java settings in Prism Launcher
observation: Prism documents Java runtimes as launch dependencies selected globally or per instance.
product_implication: Classify managed runtimes as replaceable dependencies, but keep every version still referenced by a valid instance.
quality_note: First-party Prism documentation.

title: ATLauncher runtime data appeared in a macOS temporary folder
observation: A macOS user found the jar build writing launcher runtime data under a private temporary folder while the app build failed to launch instances.
product_implication: Do not assume temporary-looking paths are disposable. Link files to a live owner process and configuration before classifying them.
quality_note: Direct first-person report in the owner issue tracker.

title: ATLauncher copied downloaded mod files into instances
observation: A macOS user observed downloaded mod jars being copied into an instance, leaving both the source download and installed copy.
product_implication: Show source downloads and installed mod copies as separate roles. Reclaim the source only after confirming import success and user intent.
quality_note: Direct first-person report in the owner issue tracker.

title: ATLauncher instances consumed about 30 GB inside the app bundle path
observation: A macOS user reported roughly 30 GB of instance data under the launcher's app-related path and asked to move it.
product_implication: Detect large mutable data stored near an app bundle and offer a verified owner-aware move, not direct folder deletion.
quality_note: Direct first-person report in the owner issue tracker.

title: ATLauncher users asked to change the instance folder
observation: A user asked for a supported way to change where launcher instances are stored.
product_implication: Prefer the owner's configured relocation path. If no owner operation exists, require copy, registration, launch, and source-removal gates.
quality_note: Direct first-person report in the owner issue tracker.

title: ATLauncher on macOS did not accept an external CurseForge download
observation: A macOS user could download a pack outside the launcher but could not get the launcher to recognize it.
product_implication: A downloaded archive is not proof of an installed pack. Keep import state explicit before labeling either copy redundant.
quality_note: Direct first-person report in the owner issue tracker.

title: A new ATLauncher install failed downloads until the user retried on another network
observation: A macOS user hit rate-limit failures during a new instance install and retried through another network.
product_implication: Treat failed or retried download trees as partial state until checksums and owner completion records prove what is usable.
quality_note: Direct first-person report in the owner issue tracker.

title: ATLauncher placed a game directory inside its macOS app contents
observation: A macOS user reported a game directory under ATLauncher.app Contents, and a launcher update disrupted the instance.
product_implication: Inspect application bundles for mutable game data, but treat discovered instances as live user state and not disposable app residue.
quality_note: Direct first-person report in the owner issue tracker.

title: A mod could not read or write in an ATLauncher macOS instance
observation: A macOS user reported that a mod could not read and write expected files inside an ATLauncher instance.
product_implication: Permission failure must not be read as absence or orphaning. Report inaccessible state and block cleanup until access is resolved.
quality_note: Direct first-person report in the owner issue tracker.

title: ATLauncher did not see requested mods in macOS Downloads
observation: A macOS user said requested mod files were present in Downloads but the launcher could not see them despite permission changes.
product_implication: A launcher inventory gap does not make the local download redundant. Distinguish filesystem presence, access, and owner recognition.
quality_note: Direct first-person report in the owner issue tracker.

title: ATLauncher file picker showed protected macOS folders as empty
observation: A macOS user saw Downloads, Documents, and Desktop as empty in the add-mod file picker even after granting broad disk access.
product_implication: Treat empty owner views of protected folders as an access problem. Never infer that the underlying files do not exist.
quality_note: Direct first-person report in the owner issue tracker.

title: Transferring a Minecraft license between devices
observation: Minecraft support separates account license access from locally stored game worlds and device data.
product_implication: Do not treat account entitlement as backup proof for worlds, screenshots, mods, or local settings.
quality_note: First-party Minecraft support documentation.

title: Troubleshooting Minecraft Launcher startup
observation: Minecraft support includes launcher and Java troubleshooting steps while warning that prior settings or modifications can affect behavior.
product_implication: Separate replaceable launcher and runtime files from user-selected mods, settings, and worlds before any reset or reinstall cleanup.
quality_note: First-party Minecraft support documentation.

title: Minecraft Java Edition hotkeys and screenshots
observation: Minecraft documents the screenshot hotkey and the creation of screenshot files during play.
product_implication: Classify screenshots below game roots as user-created media even when they sit next to replaceable game data.
quality_note: First-party Minecraft support documentation.

title: Accounts required to play Minecraft
observation: Minecraft documents the account requirements used to authenticate and access editions of the game.
product_implication: Treat authentication and entitlement as owner state. Avoid resets that sign the user out unless that consequence is explicit.
quality_note: First-party Minecraft support documentation.

title: Downloading and installing Minecraft Launcher
observation: Minecraft support documents the launcher as the owner-managed entry point for downloading and starting game versions.
product_implication: Prefer the owner's reinstall path for launcher packages while protecting game worlds, screenshots, resource packs, and settings stored nearby.
quality_note: First-party Minecraft support documentation.

title: PlayCover import reported a full disk during extraction
observation: A macOS user importing an app saw a disk-full extraction error followed by an illegal byte-sequence error.
product_implication: Classify failed extraction output as partial state. Check active handles and owner records before offering exact-path removal.
quality_note: Direct first-person report in the owner issue tracker.

title: A PlayCover game downloaded more resources after IPA installation
observation: A macOS user reached an in-game resource download after installing the IPA, showing that the installed app was not the full storage footprint.
product_implication: Scan post-install resource roots and label them separately from the app package so reclaim estimates include all owned payloads.
quality_note: Direct first-person report in the owner issue tracker.

title: Clearing PlayCover data and cache did not fix a crash
observation: A user reinstalled and cleared PlayCover data and cache, but the application still crashed.
product_implication: Do not present cache deletion as a guaranteed repair. State the storage gain and likely side effects separately from diagnostic claims.
quality_note: Direct first-person report and a useful cleanup counterexample.

title: PlayCover failed while installing an IPA
observation: A macOS user reported an error during IPA installation, leaving uncertain install state.
product_implication: Require owner success evidence before treating an archive as imported or treating partial install output as a valid game.
quality_note: Direct first-person report in the owner issue tracker.

title: A PlayCover game decompressed shaders during startup
observation: A macOS user saw a game spend startup time decompressing shaders before failing later in launch.
product_implication: Classify shader data separately from the base app. Mark it rebuildable only when the game can recreate it and no user state shares the path.
quality_note: Direct first-person report in the owner issue tracker.
